subject: Pricing follow-up — token economics & benchmarking
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up — token economics & benchmarking

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few clarification items so we can size a proposal that matches your usage: 

- Current & expected volumes: you mentioned ~100M tokens/month now with a peak of ~250M for the personalization pipeline. Can you confirm those numbers are monthly averages vs peak?
- Model footprint: you said most requests use a 2k token context with ~150 tokens generated on average. Confirm if the 2k is max context for few-shot prompting or typical usage.
- Unit economics target: you noted a goals-of-$/1M-tokens target but didn’t set a hard number. Can you share the target range for finance approval (e.g., $xxx–$yyy/1M tokens)?
- Procurement: any specific timelines or PO thresholds we should be aware of?

Next steps: if you confirm the above we’ll produce a short cost comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic and an indicative Redwood pricing deck for your expected monthly tiers (non-binding). I’ll include Aditya (SE) on the next note to align on throughput/latency targets.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0102
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-models.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — token economics & benchmarking

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. Confirming the numbers:
- Average: ~100M tokens/month (inference only).
- Peak/burst: up to ~250M tokens in heavy weeks (we'd like burst available but not always active).
- Typical request: 2k context used for ~20% of calls; most calls are ~512 tokens context. Generated tokens average ~150 per call.
- Budget target: finance is looking for something in the $15k–$35k/month band for this workload (ballpark) which maps to roughly $150–$350 per 1M tokens depending on host/discounting — but we don't have an exact target yet.
- Procurement: standard PO process; target to finish vendor selection by end of April.

If you can share a quick $/1M tokens view vs OpenAI and Anthropic and a Redwood indicative price for our volume bands, that would help us narrow down.

Alex
Director, AI Platform | Acme Analytics
alex.johnson@acme.ai | +1 212-555-0143

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — token economics & benchmarking

Alex — appreciate the clarity, that helps a lot. Attached is a short benchmarking PDF plus an XLS with tiered Redwood indicative pricing (non-binding) by monthly token bands. Highlights here: 

Benchmarking (indicative $/1M tokens):
- OpenAI (gpt-4o-like): ~$400–$700 / 1M tokens (public API, list price; enterprise discounts vary)
- Anthropic (Claude-2/3-like): ~$350–$600 / 1M tokens (public API; discounts common for committed spend)
- Major open-model hosts/self-hosted (optimized): ~$80–$300 / 1M tokens (wide range depending on quantization, batching, and provider margins)
- Redwood indicative (for Acme volume profile):
  - 0–50M/month: $320 / 1M tokens (list tier)
  - 50–200M/month: $180 / 1M tokens (committed tier)
  - 200M+/month: $120 / 1M tokens (enterprise reserved capacity + quantization gains)

Notes & assumptions:
- These numbers assume typical LLM workloads using 2k context for ~20% of calls; Redwood's batching + KV caching can substantially reduce cost for repeated prefixes (we've modeled ~15% cost reduction already).
- OpenAI/Anthropic ranges reflect public list pricing plus typical enterprise discount ranges; precise comparisons depend on model family and concurrency/latency SLOs.
- "Major open-model hosts" bucket includes managed hosts who run optimized quantized models and pass savings through; some customers achieve <$100/1M tokens with aggressive quantization and high batchability.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which Redwood tier you'd like an official quote for (50–200M or 200M+).
2) If 200M+ is relevant, we can prepare a Dedicated/Reserved proposal that includes guaranteed latency SLOs and a deeper quantization plan (Aditya can scope the latency/throughput tradeoffs).
3) I'll prepare a formal one-page cost summary and a draft MSA addendum for procurement.

Attaching: token-cost-comparison.pdf and redwood-pricing-models.xlsx (pricing by band + sample compute assumptions). Looping Marcus (CS) to help with onboarding/contract playbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: token-cost-comparison.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick items from procurement: 
- Can you send a formal quote for the 50–200M tier and a parallel quote for a 200M+ reserved capacity option (include any required commit levels and typical lead time)?
- We also need a short note on data residency/SOC2 evidence for the procurement packet (Marcus, please advise).
- Target timeline: procurement wants a formal quote by next Tue (2026-03-31) to keep vendor selection on track.

Marissa/Aditya: can you confirm if the 200M+ price includes quantized model runtime and whether that impacts latency (we're sensitive to p95 latency < 350ms on 512-token prompts)?

Alex
